title: Variables in Stored Procedures
description: Learn how to declare variables, assign values, and use them in queries within stored procedures.

data.text: Variables in SQL Server Stored Procedures

A variable is an object that holds a single value of a specific type such as integer, date, or varying character string. Variables are commonly used as loop counters, to hold values for control-of-flow statements, and to store return values.

data.title: DECLARE a single variable
data.content: Declares a variable with a data type.

data.title: DECLARE multiple variables
data.content: Declares multiple variables in one statement.

data.title: SET a variable value
data.content: Assigns a value to a variable using SET.

data.title: Variable in WHERE clause
data.content: Uses a variable to filter products by model year.
data.code:
DECLARE @model_year SMALLINT;

SET @model_year = 2018;

SELECT
    product_name,
    model_year,
    list_price
FROM
    production.products
WHERE
    model_year = @model_year
ORDER BY
    product_name;

data.title: Store COUNT result in variable
data.content: Assigns a query result to a variable.

data.title: Variables Key Points
points: Variables are declared with DECLARE and start with @.
Use SET to assign values to variables.
Variables can be used in WHERE clauses and SELECT lists.
PRINT and SELECT can display variable values.
SET NOCOUNT ON hides row-count messages.
